The full noncompact homogeneous value alternatives are retained separately:
items.reason: Scope remark: Theorem 7.A (C/07_H/heading/001) concludes objective values only and asserts no bound on the iterates; whether zero-value iterates converge in recurrent dimension ≥ 3 is open (C/07_H/prose/018, Ch07H.ZeroValueIterateQuestion); parallel of C/07_H/prose/019 and C/01_I/prose/011. Read as a claim that some run on a degree-one homogeneous objective has value convergence with unbounded iterates, the sentence would assert more than is known (no such run is constructed in Chapter 7, and for finite max-linear objectives of recurrent dimension at most two the iterates converge, C/07_H/prose/016); it is not refuted either, so it is no discrepancy. Illustration of the general non-implication behind the remark, outside the homogeneous class: ResearchStory.value_convergence_unbounded_iterates (F = eˣ: every admissible run has F(x_k) → inf F while x_k → −∞). Wording point: 'value convergence does not imply bounded iterates, and it does not subsume' (research_story.tex:31, one occurrence) → 'they conclude objective-value convergence without any conclusion about the iterates, and they do not subsume' (direct edit).
